questions.title: why doesn’t token‑level importance weighting satisfy off‑policy correction in grop?
questions.question_body: "In grop every generated response y is split into \(|y|\) tokens \(y_t\). The objective uses ratios \(w_t=\frac{\pi_\theta(y_t\mid x,y_<t)}{} \times \dots\).*These weights appear pointwise inside a min/clip surrogate."\n"I understand standard importance sampling would take a trajectory­level ratio \(\frac{\pi_\theta(y\mid x)}{}{}\).*Can anyone explain how applying \(w_t\)*pointwise* breaks proper off-policy correction and give an example where this formulation introduces bias or exploding gradients?

questions.title: what role does length­normalization play in defining \(s_i\)
questions.question_body: "GSOP defines \(s_i=\left(\frac{\pi_\theta(y}\mid x)}{}{}\right)^{\frac1{|y|}} = \exp[\frac1{|y|}\sum_t \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y_t\mid x,y_<t)}{}{}]."\n"Why divide by \(|y|\)? How does this normalize variance or affect numerical bounds?”
